items.note: S1.3 states the W-wire network on 3-subsets of [100] giving (X,Y)->(-Y,X) with restored scratch; sub-steps follow the proof: net change (JV+RG)x independent of scratch, central coefficients |S∩T| mod 2 or (|S∩T|-1)/2 with side cancellation, and the three-stage composition (741-765). Wire counts and N are not given, but these are not part of the derivation's logic.

S1.4 states the frames, the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, and the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, with the quoted reason that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate (812). It is an infer step with no sub-derivation, so it is not credited as derived.

S1.5 gives nondegenerate labels in the m-dimensional F^{⊗3}, nested labels on every edge, only central-wire decreases (quote: loss h), and the sum Wm-2N+2L with L<N/2, all matching 997-1010 and 1105-1110. L=Ich, the explicit ratios 100/539 and 101/539, and the orthonormal-basis clause are not given, and the label construction is not derived.

S1.7.4 states the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and the resulting shear H<-H+D on every role, and S1.6 gives s<Wm. The rank formula s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, the projection assignment P_U with -P_{U_a} at sources, and the rank-equals-dimension-change fact (1156-1167) are missing.

S2.2 says each edge factors into one translation kernel per orthonormal residual vector, giving s child calls in total and C^{⊗e} on every role, which agrees with 1214-1229. The frame C_U=H^{⊗m}diag(i^{q_U})H^{⊗m}, the value s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c and the diagonal endpoint corrections are not stated.
S1.6 states s<Wm for both networks and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, matching 1339-1344. The deficits eta_b and eta_c, the bound eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, which give the exponent, are not stated.
S1.1 and S1.2 restate Lemmas elementary-streams and ordered-affine-streams faithfully. The b^{O(1)} offset condition is carried by S1.2's quote, though not by its claim.

S1.7.1 states A=E_1 Pi E_2 with exactly a ones, and S1.7.2 states exactly a interchanges plus O(V). The plan does not show the elimination proof or the step H_i<-H_i+D_j realized by one interchange between two controlled updates (1432-1446).

The method and sub-steps follow the proof of Proposition power-interchange: cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, frames Phi_M, edges via matrix shears with recursive interchanges, H<-H+D from the endpoint identity, two linear updates for the interchange, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and the depth-first parking schedule with O(V) per node.

S1 states the O(Vu^tau) bound. Its method and S1.8 give the paper's reduction: high digits as the row field, padding to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces sent to the power-width procedure, and padding binary ranges to [q^e]. This is brief but follows 1649-1734.

S2.2 gives exactly s child calls on f=e/m axes after binary basis changes, with C^{⊗e} at the endpoints (1903-1916); S2.3 gives H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D (1929-1931); S2.1 gives C^{-1}=-iZCZ. The conjugation by P_M and the rule that an inverse child needs one forward call ((C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z^{⊗f} C^{⊗f} Z^{⊗f}) are not spelled out.

S2.4 gives eight packed cyclic shifts plus a sort-based repair of an exceptional set, at cost O(V(L^tau+1)). It omits delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}} and the full time bound, and it does not say that O(V(L^tau+1)) holds only in the restricted parameter family (2007-2010).

S2.5 states F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) from V/W child streams, which is correct. 'Unrolls to O(d^{lambda'})' omits the leaves F(e)=O(e) for e<d^beta, the condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda', and the row index taken from the first q_0 chunks.

The route is the paper's: the H_0 layer as b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D, the complex network with phase frames, packed basis changes, the row-split recurrence, exact guard bits, and one truncation with error below sqrt2*2^{-p}. Essential pieces are missing: where the rows come from (individual kernels on the first q_0 chunks, 2306-2323) and the arithmetic-depth recurrence that yields Delta=o(p). S2.6 only asserts Delta.

S3.1 gives B_tF_t^- in bit-reversed order and F_t^+B_t^{-1}, and S3.2 gives the error and cost. F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I is missing, and so are the exact counterparts LBF_t^- and F_t^+B^{-1}L^{-1}. S3.2 also oversimplifies: the rounds on prefix slots are processed individually, not as simultaneous layers (3115-3138).
S3.4 gives signed Kronecker substitution with four calls to the established multiplier, the exact product, and Q_p(fg/r) in O(rp log(rp)). B_0=2^{4p} and the centered residues are not given.

Error sqrt2*M(3l+1)2^{-p} and the cost are as in the proposition. The route matches: two forward transforms, pointwise products in the retained LB order (they commute with that order), one opposite transform, contraction errors added, and the exact scale by M.

S4.1 gives P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA with contractions, error below p^2, and time O(tp^{3/2+delta}alpha). 'Enough separation' replaces theta=t/s-1>p/alpha^4, and P_s, P_t are not defined. S4.2 gives the tensor identity but not gamma=2d alpha^2 or the axis-exposure cost O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)).
Both identities are stated exactly as in Lemma chirp-permutation (eq:permuted-chirp, eq:source-permutation-cancel).

S10 gives tau, lambda', c, epsilon and V=Tp=Theta(n). S5 gives the prime window (1-2eta)t_i<s_i<=(1-eta)t_i with T/2<S<T. The size choices b=ceil(log2 n), p=6b, d, K, r, alpha and eta=1/(4d), and the values of lambda, delta and kappa's role, are mostly absent.

S7 states that Phi: x->prod x_i^{mu_i} is a convolution-preserving isomorphism implemented by triangular controlled shifts, with the right cost. mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i is never defined, and the triangular formula is not given.
S8 gives the twist by zeta^k, zeta=e^{pi i/r}, the passage to C[y]/(y^r+1), and the correct wrap sign.

S4 gives the source transform as 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A and S9 the pipeline (Phi, two source transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform, rescaling, rounding, carries). S9.1 explains the two scalings by S. The digit scaling 2^{-b-2} and the definition of F^+ by conjugation are omitted.

Route: exact counterpart (u*v)/S^2, contraction errors that add for disk operands, a final bound 448b*2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding, and carries, which matches the paper. The error chain (E_s=9*2^gamma TL, E_w<28*2^gamma T^2L, the disk margins, and gamma<=b/4) is missing, so the final bound is asserted rather than obtained.

S10 says every normalized cost term is at most p^{1-2kappa}, giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), and S11 adds the schoolbook cutoff. The seven cost terms and their margins (min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa) are not listed.
S12 gives T_A(n)/(n lg n)->0, which refutes an eventual Omega(n lg n) bound in the fixed multitape model, as in 379-387.

errors.says: The layout puts the bits of all axes at common offsets in consecutive K-bit chunks, so each round is one simultaneous layer plus a recordwise twiddle shift.
errors.paper: Only rounds on chunk positions use the simultaneous-layer procedure. Rounds on prefix slots are processed individually, with bit moves and pairwise half-sum and half-difference scans, at total cost O(TpdK) (3115-3138).

errors.says: Motivation: the network turns one shear of width mf into s shears of width f on streams of volume V/W.
errors.paper: The recursive calls are interchanges of b-digit fields, one per unit of rational rank (1406-1407, 1543). The shear H<-H+D is built from these interchanges and is not itself what recurses.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: the bank-exchange network, frames, labels and the rank saving lead to the power-width interchange recurrence (S1.7) and the butterfly-layer recurrence (S2.5), which feed the synthetic transforms, resampling, chirp, CRT and twist reductions, exact recovery, and the cost table (S10). The derivation thins out at the saving itself: S1.5 and S1.6 assert Wm-2N+2L, L<N/2 and s<Wm, but nothing turns label dimensions into edge ranks (P_V-P_U, the N rank-one source edges, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b), and the exponent tau=1-2^{-50} is stated without the eta argument. The guard-width and error-chain computations are also only asserted.

steps.note: The plan gives h=100 triples, data banks, (X,Y)->(-Y,X) and restoration of every auxiliary wire. N=binom(h,3)^3 is never defined, and m=h^3 appears only implicitly, as the dimension of F^{⊗3} in S1.5.
Common frame per gate, edges D_vD_u^{-1}, commutation with pointwise gates, and the implemented operator D_out S D_in^{-1}, so only endpoint frames matter.
Nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional F^{⊗3}, comparable labels on every edge, and only central-wire edges decreasing. Its quote gives time 3 to 4 and a loss of h.
S1.6 speaks of 'rational edge ranks' but never says that rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, and never mentions the N rank-one source edges 2P_{U_a}.
The label sum Wm-2N+2L is stated, but L=Ich and the rank total s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, which carries the +N from the source edges, are missing.
L<N/2 and s<Wm both appear, but the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 do not, and the deficit N-2L>0 that links the two is not given because s_b is never expressed. Marked conservatively.
S1.7.4 states M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and the resulting shear H<-H+D on every role, scratch rows included. The projection matrices behind it are not given.
E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones, exactly a interchanges plus O(V) per edge, and s recursive calls in all.
Children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, and F_k=O(e^tau) are all present. Why s/W<m^tau holds (eta>20*2^{-50}, log m<20) is not given.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the network, the frames, the labels, the endpoint identity, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence. The middle of the chain is thin. It never shows that an edge's rank equals its label's dimension change, apart from the N rank-one source edges. Without that, the passage from the label budget Wm-2N+2L with L<N/2 to s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m is asserted rather than reconstructed.
